page: Microsoft Azure D2ls_v7 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the Dlsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is configured with 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The system allocates 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB memory-per-core ratio. The processor features a 480 MB L3 cache, a 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8). This instance does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, relying instead on external premium storage options.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is rated as average with a score of 2096.98, and single-threaded compression tasks like gzip and bzip3 decompression also perform in the average range. However, multi-core performance is constrained, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 2102.48, which falls into the bottom 10% of tested systems. Memory performance is also limited; read-only large block bandwidth is 22.83 GB/sec, and write large block bandwidth is 11.59 GB/sec, both categorized as weak or poor. Passmark CPU and memory scores reflect these resource constraints, placing the instance in the bottom 25% for general computational and database operations.

Given its low memory allocation of 4.0 GB and the lack of local storage, the D2ls_v7 represents an entry-level, compute-focused option within its family. It offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring dedicated high-clock CPU execution without massive memory footprints. However, the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and poor multi-core scaling make it unsuitable for memory-intensive databases or heavy multi-threaded processing. Appropriate workloads include lightweight single-threaded applications, basic web serving, small-scale text processing, and low-complexity microservices.
